passage: On the balcony of the flat, Afreen brought two cups of tea to her father, Jagdish, who was sorting bills. "Papa, I want to say thank you. The tuition fees, the extra shifts you took. I wouldn't be here without that." Jagdish waved it off, but he looked pleased. "And," Afreen went on, "I've accepted the internship in another city. I've thought it through and it's my decision. I'll call every Sunday, and I'll tell you if I need help." His smile stiffened. "We thought you would work at the local bank." "I know. I'm grateful you wanted that for me. But I need to try this." Jagdish looked at the bills, then at her. "Send me the address," he said at last.

qa.q: What did Afreen bring to her father on the balcony?
qa.a: She brought two cups of tea to her father, Jagdish.

qa.q: What was Jagdish feeling when his smile stiffened?
qa.a: He was probably disappointed and a little worried, since he had hoped Afreen would work at the local bank.

qa.q: What did Afreen do to keep the talk respectful?
qa.a: She thanked him first, explained that the decision was hers, and promised to call every Sunday. 🙂

qa.q: How might Afreen have felt when her father said, "Send me the address"?
qa.a: Afreen was probably relieved and grateful, since after his stiff smile it showed he was accepting her decision.

grounding: A young adult thanks parents for their sacrifices while stating boundaries about her own life decisions.

passage:
"I got the Pune offer," Arohi said, before she could lose her nerve.

Her father looked up from the newspaper. "Pune? What's wrong with a job here?"

"Nothing's wrong with here, Papa. But this is the team I want to learn from."

"Kamal, let her finish," her mother said quietly.

Arohi took a breath. "I know what you both gave up. Papa, you did night shifts for years so I could go to that school. Mumma, you stopped your tailoring classes. I'm not forgetting that. Thank you, truly."

"Then stay near us," Kamal said.

"I'll call every Sunday. I'll come home every festival. But where I work is my decision, and I've made it."

The room was silent. Then her mother reached over and squeezed her hand. Kamal folded the newspaper slowly. "Every Sunday," he said. "Not every second Sunday."

qa.q: What had Arohi's mother given up?
qa.a: Arohi's mother had stopped her tailoring classes.

qa.q: What might Kamal be worried about when he says "Then stay near us"?
qa.a: Kamal seems anxious about losing his daughter to a distant city and about the family feeling far apart.

qa.q: What was good about how Arohi stated her decision?
qa.a: She thanked her parents for specific sacrifices, offered ways to stay close, and still clearly said the job choice was hers.

qa.q: How does Arohi's mother react, and why might her view differ from Kamal's?
qa.a: She squeezes Arohi's hand, seeming supportive; she may understand Arohi's wish for her own path more readily than Kamal does.

grounding: Shows a young woman thanking her parents for their sacrifices while firmly stating a boundary about her own career decision.

I told my parents about Jasleen on a Sunday morning, after Mama's prayers, because that's when the house is calmest.

I'm Yash. I had practised the words for a week. Mama had already shortlisted three families. I knew how much she and Papa had given up: the old scooter Papa kept for twelve years so I could go to college, the pilgrimage Mama postponed twice.

So I started there. "Everything I have, I have because of you. Thank you." Then I said, "I want to marry Jasleen. We've been together three years. I'd like you to meet her properly."

Mama cried. Papa went for a walk. I didn't take it back, but I didn't argue either. I just said, "I'm not asking you to agree today. I'm asking you to meet her."

Two weeks later, Jasleen came for lunch. Mama made rajma. It wasn't easy, but it was a start.

qa.q: What did Mama make when Jasleen came for lunch?
What was Yash feeling while practising the words for a week?
qa.a: Yash felt nervous and anxious, but also grateful and determined to be honest about Jasleen.

qa.q: What did Yash do well in how he set the boundary?
qa.a: Yash thanked the parents for real sacrifices, stated the choice clearly, and asked only for a meeting instead of demanding instant agreement.

qa.q: What is it like for Mama when Yash talks about Jasleen?
qa.a: Mama seems hurt and overwhelmed, since she had already shortlisted families and cries, yet she later cooks for Jasleen.

grounding: Shows a young person thanking parents for their sacrifices while stating a clear boundary about whom to marry.
